The user wants me to decide eligibility for four benefits for a household based on the given rules and facts. I need to output JSON with decisions for each benefit.

Weekly income £154.61 (from two sources, both 2026). He receives no pension credit, no housing benefit, no DLA/PIP, no qualifying benefit on WHD date. He is liable for council tax, annual net £1,455.46. He needs care help for 9 months, day and night. Electricity bill in his name.

Now evaluate each benefit.

1. Pension Credit (Guarantee Credit)
Rules: PC-1: Claimant must live in England, Scotland, or Wales and have reached State Pension age. He lives in England (F3, F18), age 67 > 66 (F25, F26). So condition met.
PC-2: Claimant must include partner; both partners must have reached State Pension age. He has no partner (F4, F15, F22). So condition met (no partner).
PC-3: Savings up to £10,000 ignored; above that, every £500 or part thereof counts as £1 weekly income. Savings £1,614 < £10,000, so ignored.
PC-4: Guarantee Credit tops up weekly income to £238 (single) or £363.25 (couple); eligible if assessed income below threshold. He is single, threshold £238. Assessed weekly income: £154.61 (from F6, F13). Savings ignored. So assessed income £154.61 < £238. Eligible.
PC-5: Weekly Guarantee Credit amount is the difference between the threshold and assessed weekly income. So amount = £238 - £154.61 = £83.39 per week.
Thus eligible, weekly amount £83.39.

But need to check if any other income? Only weekly_income_total given. No other income mentioned. So eligible.

2. Attendance Allowance
Rules: AA-1: Must have reached State Pension age. Yes, age 67.
AA-2: Must have a physical or mental disability or health condition severe enough to need help with personal care or supervision. F19: needs_care_help = yes. So condition met.
AA-3: Must have needed that help for at least 6 months. F20: care_need_months = 9. So condition met.
AA-4: Must have been in Great Britain for at least 2 of the last 3 years. F5: in_gb_2_of_last_3_years = yes. Condition met.
AA-5: Cannot get Attendance Allowance if already receiving DLA, PIP, or Adult Disability Payment. F9: receives_dla_or_pip = no. Condition met.
AA-6: Paid at £76.70/week (lower rate) or £114.60/week (higher rate); higher rate when help needed both day and night. F21: care_day_and_night = yes. So higher rate applies: £114.60/week.
AA-7: Scheme covers England and Wales; people in Scotland apply for Pension Age Disability Payment. He is in England, so covered.
Thus eligible, weekly amount £114.60.

3. Council Tax Reduction (pensioners)
Rules: CTR-1: Council Tax Reduction available to people on low income or claiming benefits, up to 100% reduction. Model covers pensioners in England and Wales.
CTR-2: Pensioner scheme applies to people who have reached State Pension age. Yes.
CTR-3: Applicant must be liable to pay council tax on the home they live in. F16: council_tax_liable = yes. Condition met.
CTR-4: People who get the Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get maximum reduction (100% of net council tax charge). He does not currently receive Pension Credit (F7: receives_pension_credit = no). But we just determined he is eligible for Pension Credit Guarantee Credit. However, the rule says "People who get the Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get the maximum reduction". Does that mean they must be actually receiving it, or eligible? The rule says "get". Usually, if they are entitled to Guarantee Credit, they get maximum CTR. But the rule might require actual receipt. However, the rule CTR-6 says "Otherwise, people with capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction. Otherwise, the weekly reduction is the weekly net council tax charge... The household is eligible if the weekly reduction is greater than zero." So there are two paths: if they get Guarantee Credit, they get 100% reduction. Otherwise, they are assessed under CTR-6. Since he is not currently receiving Pension Credit (F7 says no), but he is eligible. The rule might be based on actual receipt. However, the assessment is for eligibility for CTR. The rule CTR-4 says "People who get the Guarantee Credit of Pension Credit get the maximum reduction". If he is not getting it, then he falls under CTR-6. But he might be eligible for Guarantee Credit, but not yet claimed. The rule doesn't say "entitled to", it says "get". So we must use CTR-6.

CTR-5: Otherwise, people with capital above £16,000 cannot get a reduction. His savings £1,614 < £16,000, so okay.
CTR-6: Otherwise, the weekly reduction is the weekly net council tax charge (annual net charge divided by 52), less 20% of any weekly income above the applicable amount.
